default_exit._why: one exit for every family so rules compete on the same footing; the owner will decide the demo stop/take-profit later and this block changes then (a change = a new screen run, its variants counted again)
default_exit._fills: signal at the close of bar t; market order at the open of the 1-minute bar that starts at t's close (+ slippage); every 1-minute bar from the entry minute on: stop first (fills at the stop or the gap open, - slippage), then the target (a limit: needs a trade 1 tick through, fills at the target); time exit at the open of the first minute at or after entry + max_hold_min; flat at the session's flatten time; one position at a time; at most max_entries_per_session entries per session

E-488.title: Multi-day channel wick poke rejection
E-488.hypothesis: Swing traders rest orders at the high/low of the last 5-20 sessions; a bar that reaches that edge, prints a long wick and closes against it has met that size, so fade back from the edge.

E-489.title: Opening-range midpoint cross with VWAP
E-489.hypothesis: The midpoint of the opening range is the opening auction's balance; once the range is complete, a close that crosses it on the VWAP side shows the day's participants leaning that way, so follow.

E-490.title: VWAP cross-count chop fade
E-490.hypothesis: When price has already crossed the VWAP several times in the last window, VWAP acts as a magnet inside a two-sided rotation; the next cross is noise that rotational traders lean against, so fade it.

E-491.title: Higher-high streak end fade
E-491.hypothesis: After several bars in a row printing higher highs (lower lows), a bar that fails to extend and closes against the streak shows the chasing buyers (sellers) are exhausted; fade it.

E-492.title: Record-range bar closing at its extreme follow
E-492.hypothesis: A bar with the widest range of the session so far that closes in the top (bottom) of its range is an unusually aggressive one-sided order flow that the book could not absorb; follow it.

E-493.title: Historical VWAP-deviation extreme fade
E-493.hypothesis: Measured against the distribution of VWAP distances seen in the previous 20 sessions, a close several standard deviations from today's VWAP is a stretch intraday traders have repeatedly sold (bought); fade.

E-494.title: Price-volume correlation follow
E-494.hypothesis: When bar price changes correlate positively with volume, up moves are traded heavily and down moves lightly: aggressive buyers dominate; follow the sign when the correlation turns strongly one way.

E-495.title: Volatility-burst extreme break follow
E-495.hypothesis: When the average range of the last few minutes jumps well above the last hour's, new information or a large parent order is moving the market; a close beyond the burst window's extreme is followed.

E-496.title: Bar-colour dominance follow
E-496.hypothesis: When most bars of the last window close up (down) and the net move agrees, a steady stream of small marketable orders is lifting offers (hitting bids) rather than one big print; follow it.

E-497.title: Prior-session central pivot hold-cross follow
E-497.hypothesis: The prior session's central pivot (H+L+C)/3 is a reference many desks publish; a run of closes that stays beyond it means the day accepted the new side, so follow the first such confirmed cross.
